1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Animal Apocalypse (1 Enoch 85-90) (c. 150 BC)

The Animal Apocalypse opens with Enoch's vision of human history under the symbolism of animals: 'I saw in my vision how a bull came forth from the earth, and that bull was white' — Adam as the white bull. The entire patriarchal-Mosaic-monarchic-exilic-Hasmonean history is then narrated in animal allegory (humans as animals, angels as men, the elect as sheep, the wicked as wolves and other predators). This is the most extensive surviving pre-Christian Jewish historical-prophetic allegory; its inclusion in the Tewahedo canon gives the Ethiopian Christian historical imagination a unique typological grammar that Western Christianity (lacking the text) cannot access.

1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Animal Apocalypse (1 Enoch 85-90) (c. 150 BC)

'I saw with mine eyes as I slept, and saw the heaven above, and behold a star fell from heaven, and it arose and ate and pastured. And after that I saw the large and the black cattle, and behold all of them changed their stalls and pastures and their cattle, and began to live with each other' — Adam introduced as a WHITE BULL. The Animal Apocalypse's foundational allegorical code: humans-as-bovines, with colour-coding for righteousness (white = righteous; black = wicked; red = mixed). Tewahedo allegorical exegesis preserves the Adamic-white-bull image as the iconographic anchor for the eschatological reunification at 90:37-38.

1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Animal Apocalypse (1 Enoch 85-90) (c. 150 BC)

'And, behold, a calf was born of that white bull, and with it were born other calves, one of them white and the other black. And that first calf smote the white one and pursued him, and I saw till that white calf disappeared' — Cain (black) kills Abel (white). The allegorical structure sets up the dual-line genealogy that runs through the entire Animal Apocalypse: a white line (righteous Sethite-Noachic-Abrahamic descent) and a black line (Cainite wickedness). Tewahedo homilies on Cain/Abel preserve this colour-coded allegorical structure.
